chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr who said:
For every thing there is a zakat, and the zakat of bodies is the fast.

key_terms.الأجساد: Bodies (plural of jism) — the physical human body, emphasizing the somatic dimension of spiritual practice
key_terms.الصوم: Sawm (fasting) — the act of abstaining from food, drink, and other specified matters from dawn to sunset
key_terms.زكاة: Zakat — literally 'purification/growth'; the obligatory alms-tax in Islamic law, but here used metaphorically to mean the purifying practice due from each category of creation

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat of the body in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain from Musa ibn Bakr (a companion of Imam al-Kazim), presents fasting as the 'zakat' — the purifying alms — of the body. Just as financial zakat purifies wealth and the soul, sawm (fasting) serves as the means of bodily purification and discipline. The original audience would have understood this as establishing fasting's obligatory and purifying character parallel to the financial duty of zakat.
